en.s: Hlöðr now grew very angry at being called a bondwoman's child and a bastard if he accepted his brother's offer, and at once he turned away with all his men, until he came home to Húnaland to King Humli, his kinsman, and told him that Angantýr, his brother, had refused him an equal share. Humli now asks about all their talk. He then became very angry that Hlöðr, his daughter's son, should be called a slave-woman's son, and then said:

l: Well shall we, Hlöðr, for you

on.s: Þenna vetr sátu þeir Humli ok Hlöðr um kyrrt. Um várit drógu þeir her saman svá mikinn, at aleyða var eftir vígra manna í Húnalandi.... Sem þessi herr kom saman, riðu þeir skóg þann, er Myrkviðr heitir, er skilr Húnaland ok Gotaland. En sem þeir kómu af skóginum, þá váru byggðir stórar ok vellir sléttir, ok á völlunum stóð borg ein fögr, en þar réð fyrir Hervör, systir Angantýs konungs, ok Ormarr, fóstri hennar. Váru þau sett þar til landgæzlu fyrir her Húna, ok höfðu þau þar mikit lið. Þat var einn morgun í sólar upprás, at Hervör stóð upp á kastala einum yfir borgarhliði. Hon sá jóreyki stóra suðr til skógarins, svá at löngum fal sólina. Því næst sá hon glóa undir jóreyknum, sem á gull eitt liti, fagra skjöldu ok gulli lagða, gyllta hjalma ok hvítar brynjur. Sá hon þá, at þetta var herr Húna ok mikill fjölði. Hervör gekk ofan skyndiliga ok kallar lúðrsvein ok bað blása saman lið. en.s: That winter Humli and Hlöðr sat quiet. In the spring they gathered so great an army that Húnaland was left empty of fighting men.... When this army had come together, they rode through the forest called Myrkviðr, which divides Húnaland and Gotaland. And when they came out of the forest, there were large settlements and level plains, and on the plains stood a fair fortress, and Hervör, sister of King Angantýr, ruled there, with Ormarr, her foster-father. They had been set there to guard the land against the army of the Huns, and they had a great force there. One morning at sunrise Hervör stood up on a tower above the fortress gate. She saw great clouds of dust from horses south towards the forest, so that they hid the sun for a long time. Next she saw a gleam beneath the dust-cloud, as if one looked on gold: fair shields overlaid with gold, gilded helmets and white mail-coats. She then saw that this was the army of the Huns, and a great multitude. Hervör went down quickly and calls a trumpeter and bade him sound the assembly of the troops. And then Hervör said: "Take your weapons and make ready for battle, and you, Ormarr, ride against the Huns and offer them battle before the southern gate of the fortress." Ormarr said:

l: for the peoples of the Goths

on.s: Þá reið Ormarr af borginni ok í mót hernum. Hann kallaði hátt ok bað þá ríða til borgarinnar, -- "ok úti fyrir borgarhliðinu suðr á völlinn -- þar býð ek yðr til orrostu. Bíði þeir þar annarra, er fyrr koma." Nú reið Ormarr aftr til borgarinnar, ok var Hervör þá albúin ok allr herr. Riðu þau nú út af borginni með hernum móti Húnum, ok hófsk þar allmikil orrosta. en.s: Then Ormarr rode out of the fortress and towards the army. He called loudly and bade them ride to the fortress, "and outside before the fortress gate, south on the plain, there I offer you battle. Let those who come first wait there for the others." Now Ormarr rode back to the fortress, and Hervör was then fully ready, and the whole army. They now rode out of the fortress with the army against the Huns, and a very great battle began there. But since the Huns had a much larger force, the losses turned against Hervör's side, and at last Hervör fell and a great host around her. And when Ormarr saw her fall, he fled, and all those who saved their lives. Ormarr rode day and night, as fast as he could, to meet King Angantýr in Árheimar. .... And when Ormarr came before King Angantýr, he said:

on.s: Angantýr spyrr nú til Húna hers. Þá sendi hann alla vegu menn frá sér ok stefndi hverjum manni til sín, er honum vildi lið veita ok vápnum mætti valda. Fór hann þá á Dúnheiði með lið sitt, ok var þat allmikill herr. Kom þá á móti honum herr Húna, ok höfðu þeir lið hálfu fleira. At öðrum degi hófu þeir sína orrostu ok börðust allan þann dag ok fóru at kveldi í herbúðir sínar. Þeir börðust svá átta daga, at höfðingjar váru enn heilir, en engi vissi manntal, hvat margt fell. En bæði dag ok nótt dreif lið til Angantýs af öllum vegum, ok þá kom svá, at hann hafði eigi færa fólk en í fyrstu. Varð nú orrostan enn ákafari. Váru Húnar allákafir ok sá þá sinn kost, at sú ein var lífs ván, ef þeir sigruðust, ok illt mundi Gota griða at biðja. Gotar vörðu frelsi sitt ok fóstrjörð fyrir Húnum, stóðu því fast, ok eggjaði hverr annan. Þá er á leið daginn, gerðu Gotar atgöngu svá harða, at fylkingar Húna svignuðu fyrir.
